title: A · 疏朗阔叶
prompt:
Create a vegetation design study for the same miniature-planet civilization-management game as the reference. Use the reference only for its soft semi-realistic stylized 3D lighting, crafted wooden/thatch building materials, natural greens and miniature scale. The existing dense fine-grained trees in the reference are the problem to REDESIGN, not the foliage style to copy.

Landscape 1536 x 1024 design plate on a clean warm ivory-gray background. No writing or graphics. Two clearly separated but visually cohesive subjects in one image: on the LEFT about 40 percent of the frame, a single complete specimen tree on a small simple grass-and-soil base with its whole root-to-canopy silhouette visible; on the RIGHT about 60 percent, a small woodland worksite on a gently convex patch of the planet's ground. The single specimen on the left is at a closer viewing scale, while the right-hand patch shows the same tree design instanced at gameplay scale. A single small thatch-roof cottage beside the left specimen is included ONLY as a consistent size reference: the tree should be about 1.35 to 1.5 times the cottage's roof-ridge height. Keep that tree-to-house relationship consistent across all studies. The cottage is visually secondary and uses the reference's simple rural architecture.

On the RIGHT, show exactly FIVE living trees in TWO loose groups, one group of three and one group of two, with a clearly visible winding dirt access lane between the groups leading to one small open logging lean-to at the front edge. Show two simple tree stumps, an orderly stack of cut logs near the lean-to, and one tiny automatic worker carrying timber as scale context. No extra houses or facilities on this woodland patch. There are real walkable spaces between tree trunks. Low shrubs appear only as a few isolated small ground accents, below knee height, never as another blanket over the woodland floor. Tree roots visibly contact the ground, and each tree stands outward perpendicular to its own part of the curved terrain.

Across BOTH subjects: clearly exposed warm brown trunk in approximately the lower third of tree height; readable main fork and a few substantial branches; canopy organized into THREE TO FIVE broad irregular foliage masses with intentional air gaps and a natural varied outline. Each foliage mass has restrained leaf-surface variation and soft light, never hundreds of tiny bead-like bumps. We should see one tree's structure at a glance. Foreground trees do not merge into neighboring crowns. No moss carpet, no cauliflower/broccoli texture, no dense ornamental shrub carpet, no spherical lollipop balls, no smooth plastic toy canopy, no flat-shaded triangle mosaic, no photorealistic microscopic leaves, no oversized bonsai sculpture. Keep the feeling softly natural and game-readable. Bark texture is subtle; strong shape and light organize the tree. Gentle warm daylight, soft shadows, controlled material detail. No extreme depth of field; all functional forms stay clear. No UI, arrows, numbers, lettering, title, logo, border, watermark, or artist signature. No large water body. The design plate is a game asset and small worksite study, not a full planet.

SPECIFIC CANOPY DESIGN FOR THIS VARIANT:
A balanced medium-height deciduous broadleaf tree with an asymmetric oval crown. One gently tapering trunk divides into two readable main branches; three to four substantial irregular foliage groups follow those branches, with a small visible opening in the center and space beneath the crown. Lower crown edge is clean and high enough to reveal the trunk and the worksite. Natural sage and oak-green hues with a few warm sunlit patches. Prioritize a readable branching silhouette, an approachable natural miniature appearance, moderate crown width and an unobstructed logging lane. The grove should feel like a practical managed resource woodland. Each tree differs slightly in branch direction and canopy volume while clearly sharing one asset family.
